lead.label: The game story
lead.title: Florida 21, No. 11 Kentucky 14: Philo runs for 102 yards and the Gators’ defense closes it out
lead.author: Brenden Martin
lead.html:
LEXINGTON, Ky. — Florida did not score an offensive point in the first half. It left Kroger Field with a win over the No. 11 team in the country.

Aaron Philo ran for 102 yards and the go-ahead touchdown, Florida’s defense stopped Kentucky on fourth down twice in the final six minutes, and the Gators beat the Wildcats 21-14 on Saturday night before an announced crowd of 61,866.

Florida (6-4, 4-4 SEC) outscored Kentucky 19-7 after halftime. Kentucky (7-3, 5-3) did not score in the fourth quarter.

The win made Florida bowl-eligible and was the Gators’ first at Kentucky since 2019, according to FloridaGators.com.

Philo’s 2-yard touchdown run with 9:08 left put Florida ahead for good. It finished a 14-play, 67-yard drive that took 7:30 off the clock. Kahleil Jackson threw to Dallas Wilson for the two-point conversion to make it 21-14.

The game turned on the second play of the third quarter. Jayden Woods sacked Kenny Minchey for a 7-yard loss and forced a fumble, and Brendan Bett recovered at the Kentucky 30. Seven plays later Jadan Baugh scored from the 1, and Philo ran in the two-point conversion for a 10-7 lead.

Kentucky had two chances to tie. Minchey’s fourth-down pass from the Florida 25 fell incomplete with 5:29 left, and Ben Hanks III broke up the Wildcats’ last fourth-down throw with 1:28 to play.
